FOUND-001.title: Conduct Foundation Event Storm for Foundation
FOUND-001.description:
Complete the foundation by capturing domain architecture through Foundation Event Storm.

Use these commands to populate foundation.json eventStorm field:
- fspec add-foundation-bounded-context <name>
- fspec remove-foundation-bounded-context <name> [--cascade]
- fspec add-aggregate-to-foundation <context> <aggregate>
- fspec remove-aggregate-from-foundation <context> <aggregate>
- fspec add-domain-event-to-foundation <context> <event>
- fspec remove-domain-event-from-foundation <context> <event>
- fspec add-command-to-foundation <context> <command>
- fspec remove-command-from-foundation <context> <command>
- fspec show-foundation-event-storm

Why this matters:
- Establishes bounded contexts for domain-driven design
- Enables tag ontology generation from domain model
- Provides foundation for architectural documentation
- Supports EXMAP-004 tag discovery workflow

See spec/CLAUDE.md "Foundation Event Storm" section for detailed guidance.

userStory.action: map the bounded contexts, aggregates, domain events, and commands of this macOS engine port
userStory.benefit: the project foundation reflects the real domain so specs and tags stay consistent

rules.text: Foundation event storm captures the 4 bounded contexts (Deterministic Simulation, Native Graphics & Present, Build & Release Pipeline, Content Distribution & Launcher), 4 aggregates, and the core domain events

examples.text: spec/foundation.json lists the 4 bounded contexts with aggregates: SyncedState, PresentFrame, ReleaseArtifact, GameContent

show-foundation event-storm view shows the 4 bounded contexts, their aggregates (SyncedState, PresentFrame, ReleaseArtifact, GameContent), and the domain events (SyncGatePassed, FramePresented, ReleaseCertified)

SYNC-001.title: Streflop cross-arch bit-exactness gate runs and passes on every build
SYNC-001.description: tools/sync-test (streflop_float_test.cpp) exercises 52,080 streflop libm ops (denormals, branch-cut, huge/tiny) on the current arch and compares bit patterns to the committed references (streflop_results_NEON_arm64, SSE_x86_64) via compare_results.py. SYNC_VALIDATION.md: 52,080/52,080 vs NEON, 47,852/47,852 vs SSE. This is the cheapest determinism gate — must stay bit-exact on any FP/flag/compiler change. Reverse-tracked gate (existing tooling), not new code.

SYNC-002.title: Fleet libm (dbl-64) parity hash gate passes 9/9 in every release build
SYNC-002.description: The shipping build swaps the affected streflop dbl-64 objects with gcc-built ones (gcc's -fsingle-precision-constant demotes unsuffixed FP literals in streflop's double libm; clang has no equivalent, so pure-clang diverges up to ~45 ULPs in asin/acos-family results). A 9-function hash harness (scripts/dfp-small.cpp: atan2, sin, cos, tan, floor, fmod, sqrt/log, asin/acos, exp/atan chains) must match the gcc x86-64 reference 9/9; it is a mandatory release-build step (scripts/build-engine.sh + gcc-dbl64-swap.sh). A build that fails it does not ship.

SYNC-003.title: Synced-code float→short UB sweep matches fleet (gcc-x86) behavior
SYNC-003.description: Out-of-range float→short conversion is UB; clang-arm64 and gcc-x86 disagreed (real desync in Raptors via COB callin). Defined int32 truncation replacing the narrow cast in: CobInstance.cpp/CobThread.cpp (callin truncation, commit 8a041014a2 + COB fix), IPathController.cpp GetDeltaHeading, GroundMoveType/HoverAirMoveType direct-control heading, LuaSyncedMoveCtrl.SetHeading, LuaSyncedRead.GetFacingFromHeading. Complete register: docs/SYNC_VALIDATION.md Appendix A. Every one is sync-safe (changes behavior only where UB/divergence) and an upstream candidate.

userStory.action: pin the float→short UB-sweep gate test (testClampRad) to the port's defined float→int→short conversion
userStory.benefit: the whole sync-UB gate passes on arm64 with the fleet's (gcc-x86) values and no platform-dependent UB remains in the sweep or its gate

rules.text: The expected TA-short values must match the fleet's gcc-x86 behavior, which is float->int->short (cvttss2si then narrow): short(nextafter(TWOPI,-inf)*RAD2TAANG) == -1 (65536 wraps), short(ClampRadPi(-PI)*RAD2TAANG) == -32768, short(ClampRadPi(nextafter(PI,-inf))*RAD2TAANG) == 32767.

Gate test testClampRad must pin the port's DEFINED conversion (float->int32->short, as used at every sweep site in IPathController/GroundMoveType/HoverAirMoveType/LuaSyncedMoveCtrl/LuaSyncedRead/CobInstance), never a raw float->short cast: the raw cast is UB when the value leaves short's range and produced platform-dependent results (65535 vs -1) for the same bit pattern on arm64.

examples.text: testClampRad line 47: static_cast<short>(ClampRad(nextafter(TWOPI,-inf)) * RAD2TAANG) must go through int32 (the port's defined conversion) and equal short(-1); the raw cast is UB and the test currently fails with '-1 == -1' on arm64 (-O2)

Engine sweep sites already pin the defined conversion (verified present in tree): CobInstance.cpp RadAngleToCobShort short(int(radAngle*RAD2TAANG)); IPathController.cpp x3 short(int(...)); GroundMoveType.cpp UpdateDirectControl x2; HoverAirMoveType.cpp UpdateHeading x2; LuaSyncedMoveCtrl.cpp SetHeading (short)(int)luaL_checknumber; LuaSyncedRead.cpp GetFacingFromHeading (short)(int)luaL_checknumber

architectureNotes.text: Root cause of the testClampRad failure: line 47 uses a raw float→short cast, which is UB once the value leaves short's range. On arm64 -O2 the compiler lowers it to fcvtzs-with-saturation (65535.996 → 65535) which neither fits a short nor equals the fleet's value; on x86 the same expression lowers as cvttss2si-into-32-bit-then-narrow (65535 → 65535 wraps to -1). The engine's sweep already pins the defined float→int32→short form at every site (8a041014a2 + 7104ab1f76), so the gate test must use the same form. No rts/ code changes needed — engine sweep sites verified present in tree; only the test file changes.

GFX-001.title: GL_PRIMITIVE_RESTART enabled only for strip/loop/fan topologies
GFX-001.description: LuaVAOImpl force-enabled restart around every indexed draw incl. hardcoded GL_TRIANGLES Submit(); on Metal-backed GL the restart index 0xffffff forces a per-draw compute index-unroll (KK primitiveTopologyListRestart) = 94% of BAR's draws = the 6.8fps bottleneck. UsePrimitiveRestart(mode) returns true only for LINE_STRIP/LOOP, TRIANGLE_STRIP/FAN (+adjacency); SPRING_LUAVAO_FORCE_RESTART=1 restores old behavior. Commit e34e563829. 6.8→23.1 fps. Upstream candidate (upstream #1).

GFX-002.title: Native Metal present path (Zink→KosmicKrisp→Metal) renders + presents at display-class fps
GFX-002.description: GL 4.6 compat on Apple Silicon via pinned Mesa Zink + KosmicKrisp → Metal. Rebuilt present path: GPU-pack PBO-ring readback (present 30ms→~1ms, f53785f4ac), async present + double-buffered IOSurface killing the 60fps cap (35153cbb47), direct unified-memory pixel-buffer present (a1b5f573df, MacPresentDirect=1 default), 6-deep persistent-map upload ring + non-spinning 250µs fence waits (458b4152e2, SPRING_MAC_STREAM_BUFFERING), KK_MATH_MODE=fast default (2c32206212), zink renderpass tracking (patch 0013), panel-native + GPU-pixel-budget render density cap (89aa5f96dd). MacPresentBackend.mm (Platform/Mac) extracted at 895780d717. Loud failure on software-GL fallback (915127907e).

GFX-003.title: Geometry-shader stage probed at init; GS compiles refused when the stage is dead
GFX-003.description: Some drivers (incl. Metal-backed) expose a GL >= 3.2 context whose GLSL front-end compiles + links geometry shaders, but the device has no geometry stage → silently draws nothing. ProbeGeometryShaderStage() (GlobalRendering, 92085c2165) really runs a geometry shader at init and stores supportGeometryShaderStage; Shader.cpp refuses GS compiles when the stage is dead (92085c2165) and restores shader uniforms before validating a re-linked program (329cf9f974). BAR does not require GS, so refusing is correct and loud.

SYNC-004.title: streflop math::floor reproduces x86 cvttss2si saturation semantics on arm64
SYNC-004.description: Base-specific: cvtt/INT_MIN emulation (c20b863148) belongs to the 2025.06.24 lineage (v0.11/v0.12) only. On that base the official x86 fleet resolved math::floor to fastmath::floor (cvttss2si -> INT_MIN) while the mac streflop_cond.h exact-match overloads shadowed it with IEEE streflop::floor -> real desync, fixed by c20b863148. On the current 2026.07.04 base (main/v0.13, streflop submodule @570f86f, shared by upstream master's x86 pin too) both archs resolve math::floor to the same shared libm s_floorf/s_floor bit-twiddling (verified bit-exact across the committed NEON vs SSE references, 1985/1985 common inputs, 0 mismatches incl. NaN/inf edge rows). Porting the cvtt emulation to main would REINTRODUCE a desync vs the x86 fleet of this base. Deliverable here: regression guard unit test pinning the resolved IEEE-floor semantics against the committed cross-arch reference values (so a future cherry-pick of c20b863148 or a streflop pin change that adds arch-divergent floor behavior fails the gate), plus doc corrections (SYNC_VALIDATION Appendix A, this work unit).

rules.text: Base-specificity: the cvtt/INT_MIN emulation (c20b863148) is a 2025.06.24-lineage fix (v0.11/v0.12, in-tree streflop). On that base the official x86 fleet resolved math::floor to fastmath::floor (int-truncate -> cvttss2si -> INT_MIN), while the mac layer's streflop_cond.h exact-match overloads shadowed it with IEEE streflop::floor (NaN) -> real desync. On the 2026.07.04 base (main/v0.13) streflop is a submodule (570f86f) whose shared IEEE floor is bit-exact across NEON/SSE, so both archs converge on IEEE floor and the cvtt class is closed WITHOUT the emulation.

Invariant (base-scoped): on the 2026.07.04 base, math::floor(float/double) resolves via streflop_cond.h's exact-match overloads to the streflop submodule's shared libm s_floorf/s_floor bit-twiddling, which the committed cross-arch references prove bit-identical between NEON/arm64 and SSE/x86-64 (1985/1985 common inputs, 0 mismatches, including the NaN=0x7FC00000, inf=0x7F800000 and huge=0x7F7FFFFF edge rows). Any change that makes arm64 floor diverge from x86 floor (e.g. cherry-picking the 2025.06.24 cvtt emulation c20b863148 onto this base) fails this gate.

examples.text: math::floor(3.7f)==3.0f and math::floor(-3.7f)==-4.0f on both archs (probe + references agree).

math::floor(float NaN)==NaN bit 0x7FC00000 and math::floor(double NaN)==NaN (probe on arm64, NEON, engine flags; matches committed NEON reference floor(7FC00000)->7FC00000). A cvtt-style fix would make these INT_MIN (0x80000000) and fail the test.

math::floor(+3e38f)==+3e38f (bit 0x7F61B1E6) and math::floor(-3e38f)==-3e38f on both archs — huge-magnitude inputs are already integral, floor is identity; a cvtt-style path would yield INT_MIN / INT_MAX and fail.

userStory.action: verify the resolved math::floor semantics of the current 2026.07.04 base with a committed regression test
userStory.benefit: any future change that makes arm64 floor diverge from the x86 fleet (cherry-pick of the old cvtt fix, streflop pin change) fails a gate instead of desyncing live lockstep games

architectureNotes.text: Test file: test/engine/System/testFloorSemantics.cpp, Catch2, same wiring as testClampRad (test_Common_sources + streflop lib, -DNOT_USING_CREG -DBUILDING_AI). It includes lib/streflop/streflop_cond.h then System/FastMath.h (the exact include order of lmathlib.cpp, the synced Lua math.floor callin) and pins math::floor's resolved output bits for bounded/NaN/inf/out-of-range float+double inputs against the committed tools/sync-test cross-arch references (NEON vs SSE, floor 1985/1985 common inputs, 0 mismatches). No engine globals; pure function evaluation.

Evidence trail (probe /tmp/floor_probe, engine flags, STREFLOP_NEON, -ffp-contract=off): on main (2026.07.04 base) math::floor(NaN)=0x7FC00000, math::floor(±3e38)=±0x7F61B1E6, math::floor(2.25f)=0x40000000, math::floor(-0.25f)=0xBF800000; double: floor(NaN)=0x7FF8000000000000, floor(±inf)=±0x7FF0000000000000. fastmath::floor(NaN)=0 on arm64 (fcvtzs) vs INT_MIN on x86 (cvttss2si) — the one remaining arch-divergent path, but it is only reachable via direct fastmath::floor calls; no synced call site uses it (grep: only the using-declaration in FastMath.h). The cvtt fix c20b863148 is NOT on main/v0.13 and must not be cherry-picked forward (would make arm64 diverge from this base's x86 fleet).

PLAT-001.title: Retina mouse coordinate mapping lands clicks + edge-scroll in the exact pixel
PLAT-001.description: SDL emits mouse events in logical (point) coords; the engine viewport is in backing-pixel coords. Without rescaling, windowed clicks land at half the cursor position on Retina. ScaleMouseCoords maps the last reachable logical coord (sdlW-1) onto the last pixel (viewSize-1) — plain size-ratio scaling tops out 2px short of the right/bottom edge on 2x, which broke edge scrolling (engine edge tests compare against viewSize-1, issue #7). Commit 03d7a6b278. ScaleMouseDelta scales motion deltas by viewSize/sdlSize.

PLAT-002.title: EdgeMoveWidth=0 disables edge scrolling
PLAT-002.description: EdgeMoveWidth is declared minimumValue(0.0f) and documented as the % of screen for the edge-scroll band, so 0 should mean OFF. It never did: border = std::max<int>(1, w*edgeMoveWidth) floors the band to 1px, so a pointer parked at x==0 scrolled the camera indefinitely with no input (cost a perf baseline — LESSON-57). Commit 4d2977e7a8 adds an early `return v` when edgeMoveWidth <= 0 in CCamera::GetMoveVectorFromState. Not macOS-specific (any platform). Default 0.02 untouched.

PLAT-003.title: Generic log repeat-coalescer bounds infolog.txt growth
PLAT-003.description: High-frequency structurally-identical log lines (per-event [input] diagnostics, per-stall [stall] warnings) bloat infolog.txt to hundreds of MB over a long session, making it useless as a bug-report attachment. A generic repeat-coalescer in the log backend (rts/System/Log/Backend.cpp, commit b408ad288d) collapses near-identical lines at the one choke point every record passes through: up to 8 tracked signature slots (NUM_SLOTS), numeric tokens collapsed to '#' so only-varying-by-number lines share a signature, 'previous line repeated N more time(s)' rollups, LRU eviction, thread-safe with emit outside the lock. No per-source throttles needed.

userStory.role: support engineer collecting a bug report from a BAR player on a long session
userStory.action: keep the player's infolog.txt small enough to attach
userStory.benefit: the log stays a useful diagnostic instead of a hundreds-of-MB flood of structurally-identical lines

rules.text: At most NUM_SLOTS=8 tracked signatures; a new/distinct line claims a free slot else evicts the least-recently-used slot, flushing that slot's pending tail first
Signature = section + message with each numeric token collapsed to '#'; lines differing only in numbers share a signature; punctuation-only runs stay verbatim in the signature
Coalescer decisions are made under the backend mutex but sink emits happen outside it, so a re-entrant sink cannot deadlock

A matching record is suppressed and counted; every ROLLUP_EVERY=100th suppression emits a 'previous line repeated N more time(s)' rollup at the original level and section; log_backend_flushRepeats emits any residual tail

examples.text: 5 interleaved input-motion lines + 5 interleaved stall lines -> each pattern passes through once, all 8 suppressed repeats accounted in per-pattern rollups reporting their own sections
101 near-identical stall warnings (numbers vary) -> exactly 1 full line emitted, 100 suppressed, sum of rollup counts == 100, rollup carries the stall section and original level

architectureNotes.text: The coalescer is the generic mechanism that replaces per-source throttles: it sits at the log_backend_record choke point in System/Log/Backend.cpp, so every sink (console, file) benefits automatically and no call site changes. The [stall] throttle previously in GlobalRendering was removed in the same commit (b408ad288d).

Determinism contract: the coalescer affects only the logging subsystem (System/Log), which is outside the synced simulation — no behavior change under rts/Sim/ or streflop, so multiplayer bit-exactness is untouched. Thread-safety: decisions under a std::mutex, sink emits outside the lock (a sink may re-enter the logger, e.g. FileSink logging a failed fopen).

PLAT-004.title: SDL-queue gesture injection hook for unattended input verification
PLAT-004.description: OS-level input synthesis (CGEvent) cannot reach the game when the console is locked/headless, blocking unattended verification of input-driven rendering fixes. SPRING_DBG_INJECT=<path> makes InputHandler::PushEvents push a scripted gesture timeline into SDL's own event queue (real input pipeline from SDL_PollEvent onward). The GestureInjector parses a timeline file written after launch: '<t_sec> move x y' / 'down x y [button]' / 'up x y [button]' / 'wheel dy', '#' comments, y-down logical window coords, pushed in order at the next pump. Commit d9938d94be. Pair with SPRING_DBG_INPUT=1 to log every received/mapped event (input-method source, precise/pixel vs line deltas).

PLAT-005.title: Window modes, on-screen sizing, and cursor confinement on macOS
PLAT-005.description: Window modes, on-screen sizing, and edge-scroll cursor confinement on macOS. Window mode fixes (99cf5ba2ce, 20c4307b0b): coverage/input extent/display pinning for fullscreen + borderless. Persist logical (point) size not backing-pixel (b57d730651). Retina winPosY_bl corrected to use winSizeYpt (29bd947106). WindowTitle config with {version} placeholder (3a31eab517, cross-platform). Optionally show true render resolution in title (29bd947106). WindowBorderless handling (f0d789bc51, d4f2459ce4).

BUILD-001.title: One-command reproducible build + release pipeline (make app/certify/release)
BUILD-001.description: Reproducible one-command pipeline: make app (BAR launcher pkg, headless-safe) / engine / engine-dist / certify / release. packaging/release-build.sh builds the pinned Mesa Zink+KosmicKrisp driver from the pinned commit + patches/mesa/ (provenance-stamped, cached), builds the engine with the deterministic-FP config, runs the determinism gates (libm 9/9 + streflop sync-test), stages/signs/notarizes the bundle + styled DMG. Tiers mirror upstream Recoil CI (build vs validation). Commits: e240ca473b, 863c4126dc, 337cb7ed90, a49a8ecc52.

BUILD-002.title: Engine version pinned to the live-fleet release (version identity is a multiplayer requirement)
BUILD-002.description: Lockstep multiplayer requires every client to run the same engine version doing the same math. Shipping builds are made from pinned `macos-<version>` branches = the upstream release tag + the macOS layer (no stray upstream drift). ConfigureVersion.cmake prefers a PINNED_VERSION file over git-describe (f5c2f63347), then auto-derives from the nearest [0-9]* release tag (a70da5d66c) so the engine reports exactly the base release (e.g. 2026.07.04), not a dev string. docs/VERSIONS.md pins engine, Mesa commit, SPIRV-LLVM-Translator, pr-downloader, macOS floor — never bump a pin silently. Current tree is the 2026.07.04 engine lane.

LAUNCH-001.title: BAR Launcher: consent, content download/update, remote message system
LAUNCH-001.description: Drag-to-install BAR Launcher.app: explicit first-run consent dialog (default Quit, single-source content-server display, centered, disclaims responsibility), downloads Beyond All Reason from the official content network via launcher.sh (non-blocking tmutil, progress window), keeps it updated, launches into the lobby. Remote message system: versioned dialogs, version-targeted announcements + kill-switch, rich multi-button dialogs, suppression; fetched over pinned-TLS GitHub with size cap, HTML-sanitized; served from message-config/ assembled by CI. Online play enabled by default in source builds, disabled in released builds while approval is sought (server address neutralized to loopback). make test runs packaging/test/{message-check,launcher,dialog-center}-test.sh.

LAUNCH-002.title: Online play enabled: remove the online-disable machinery
LAUNCH-002.description: Remove the code that disables the ability to connect to BAR's internet/lobby servers (the 'seeking approval from the maintainers' posture): the --enable/--disable-online flags + endpoint-neutering in release-build.sh, the launcher's online-disabled notice + ack, the consent-dialog --notice mode, the Makefile ONLINE wiring, README note, and their tests. Builds connect to the real lobby by default and there is no disable switch.

userStory.action: start the game and connect to the official lobby / online play
userStory.benefit: I can play internet games against the community with no build flag or opt-in step

rules.text: The staged chobby_config.json keeps the server endpoint from the canonical dist_cfg as-is: nothing in the build or packaging path rewrites the lobby server address/port.
The build pipeline exposes no online-disable switch: --enable-online, --disable-online, BAR_ONLINE, and Makefile ONLINE= all stop existing; every packaged build ships the lobby endpoint untouched.

examples.text: A packaged build connects to the official lobby: the staged chobby_config.json keeps the exact server address+port from the canonical dist_cfg, so sign-in and the online menus reach the live servers instead of a dead loopback endpoint.

First launch of a packaged build shows no 'ONLINE PLAY IS DISABLED' notice (no .online-play-disabled marker ships, so the launcher has nothing to gate on); the remote message check and the content-disclaimer still appear as before, then the game launches.
`make app` / `make release` run without any ONLINE variable or --disable-online being passed, and the README no longer tells users to build with online play disabled.

release-build.sh given --disable-online (or --enable-online, or env BAR_ONLINE=1) refuses the argument as unknown and exits non-zero — there is no way to steer a build at the old loopback endpoint anymore.

architectureNotes.text: Deletion-only change across packaging/: release-build.sh (drop ENABLE_ONLINE + flags + neuter block), launcher.sh (drop marker gate + notice + ack), consent-dialog.swift (drop --notice mode — its only caller), Makefile (drop ONLINE var), README.md (drop disabled-release note), and the online-disabled cases in packaging/test/launcher-test.sh + dialog-center-test.sh. No new behavior; the dist_cfg endpoint becomes the shipped endpoint. Verification: bash -n on edited scripts, `make test` harnesses, and a staging dry-run asserting chobby_config.json server == dist_cfg value.

GFX-004.title: Eliminate per-unit first-spawn hitch (texture upload + shader compile deferred to first use)
GFX-004.description: When units/buildings first come into scope, the game hitches briefly. On Windows this is a few ms; on the macOS translation stack (Zink→KosmicKrisp→Metal) the same deferred work costs 10-100x more, so the pause is clearly visible. Root cause (from research): S3O model textures are decoded to CPU bitmaps at load (PreloadModels=1), but the actual GL texture upload (glTexImage2D + glGenerateMipmap) is deferred to first use via CModelLoader::Upload() → textureHandlerS3O.LoadTexture(), triggered by SolidObjectDef::LoadModel() at unit spawn (CUnit::PreInit) or first draw. New shader variants also compile at first draw of a unit type. Both run synchronously on the main thread, and the direct-present fence backpressure in MetalPresent.mm stretches one-off stalls. Fix direction: at end of CWorldDrawer::InitPost() (after DrainPreloadFutures + UploadVBOs), perform the deferred GL uploads (textureHandlerS3O.LoadTexture for every preloaded non-3DO model) so the cost moves to the load screen; optionally pre-warm common shader variants. Rendering-only: no sim impact, no determinism impact.

userStory.action: play a game without the camera freezing when new unit/building types first appear on screen
userStory.benefit: smooth, Windows-comparable gameplay through the translation stack

rules.text: Rendering-only change: nothing under rts/Sim/ or rts/lib/streflop/ changes behavior; the sync-validation gate must pass unchanged

Move first-use GL texture upload (glTexImage2D + glGenerateMipmap for S3O model textures) from first spawn to map load, executed after DrainPreloadFutures(0) + UploadVBOs() in CWorldDrawer::InitPost()
First-use of a model after the load-time bulk upload must be a no-op (uploaded flag / cached texIDs) so no code path can re-upload or desync texture state
PreloadModels=0 must keep working: the lazy first-use upload path stays intact for anything not uploaded at load time (runtime-added models, 3DO atlases, projectile visuals)
Accept longer map-load time: move the uploads to the load screen (Option A). Human approved proceeding with Option A on 2026-09-11.

Unconditional (upstreamable): applies on all platforms. It only reorders existing load-time work earlier (no new work), so the desktop load-time delta is negligible and the change stays a thin, rebaseable upstream candidate. Human approved proceeding with Option A on 2026-09-11.
Unconditional (upstreamable) — applies on all platforms; the change only reorders existing load-time work earlier. Human approved 2026-09-11.

examples.text: Map load with PreloadModels=1 on an M2-class Mac completes with all S3O model textures uploaded: textureHandlerS3O reports no texID==0 entries for preloaded models, and load time increases by a measured, reported amount (no hard budget set — target: acceptable, progress shown via SetLoadMessage)

After the fix, when the first enemy unit of a new type enters view, no [stall] draw gap >150ms line appears in the infolog and no visible camera freeze occurs (Tracy shows no Upload/LoadTexture/glGenerateMipmap span on the main thread at first spawn)
A unit with PreloadModels=0 in user settings still works: its texture uploads at first spawn exactly as before the change (lazy path intact)
Player spawns a factory and queues a first building of a new type: the building appears without a visible freeze; the (now load-time-paid) texture work does not re-run at spawn

questions.answer: Unconditional (upstreamable): applies on all platforms; only reorders existing load-time work earlier. Human approved 2026-09-11.

architectureNotes.text: Integration points: CWorldDrawer::InitPost (rts/Rendering/WorldDrawer.cpp:156-168) calls the new bulk upload after DrainPreloadFutures(0)+UploadVBOs(); CModelLoader::Upload (rts/Rendering/Models/IModelParser.cpp:462) is the per-model entry point (sets model->uploaded, releases shatter indices, runs CheckPieceNormals); CS3OTextureHandler::LoadTexture (rts/Rendering/Textures/S3OTextureHandler.cpp:106) creates the GL texIDs; first-use call sites stay unchanged (SolidObjectDef::LoadModel, UnitDrawer, UnitDrawerData) and become no-ops via the uploaded/texID caches
